pack.title: Car dealerships
pack.description: Today-only prices and trips to the manager. Decide on your timeline, not theirs.

scenarios.setting: Dealership desk. The salesperson slides the paper across and taps it.
scenarios.jab: This price is only good if you sign today.

replies.line: I'm not deciding today. I'll accept the risk it sells.
replies.why: It acknowledges possible scarcity while retaining your decision timeline.
replies.delivery: Pause, then say “I'm not deciding today” at a steady, conversational volume. ” then let the pause remain.

replies.why: Two words that end the pressure script because there's nothing to negotiate against.
replies.delivery: Say “Then no” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. ” then let the pause remain.

replies.line: I get the urgency — I still don't decide same-day. What can you do Thursday?
replies.why: It holds your buying timeline while asking whether a later offer is possible.
replies.delivery: Keep “I get the urgency” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. ” then let the pause remain.

replies.line: A price with a bedtime. Interesting. Mine sleeps in.
replies.why: It uses humor about timing while declining to decide under pressure.
replies.delivery: Keep “A price with a bedtime” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. ” then let the pause remain.

trap.line: Fine — but you're ripping me off and we both know it.
trap.why: It accepts the purchase while adding an accusation instead of holding your decision boundary.

scenarios.goal: Decline a buying deadline you cannot meet.

followUp.jab: The car really might sell today.
followUp.line: I understand; I'm prepared to miss it rather than rush.
followUp.why: It accepts genuine scarcity without allowing it to dictate your decision.
followUp.delivery: Use a relaxed pace on “prepared to miss it,” then let the pause remain.

scenarios.setting: Finance office. The manager leans back after your counteroffer.
scenarios.jab: You know what? Let me go talk to my manager. Stay right there.

replies.line: Take your time. This is the amount I'm willing to pay.
replies.why: It gives the seller space to consider your clearly stated limit.
replies.delivery: Emphasize your actual amount calmly; avoid describing their process as theater.

replies.why: It grants the trip while freezing the terms, which is the whole game.
replies.delivery: Emphasize your actual amount calmly; avoid describing their process as theater.

replies.line: Of course — tell him I'm an easy yes at my number.
replies.why: It communicates willingness to buy at your stated amount while leaving room for refusal.
replies.delivery: Emphasize your actual amount calmly; avoid describing their process as theater.

replies.line: My budget will still be here when you get back.
replies.why: Humor reinforces your limit without alleging a dishonest process.
replies.delivery: Emphasize your actual amount calmly; avoid describing their process as theater.

trap.line: Whatever — just tell me the lowest you'll actually go.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Maintain your offer while it is considered.

followUp.jab: My manager says you need to come up a little.
followUp.line: That's the amount I'm willing to pay; I can leave it with you.
followUp.why: It states your limit and allows the seller to decline.
followUp.delivery: Emphasize your actual amount calmly; avoid describing their process as theater.

scenarios.setting: After the test drive. The salesperson walks you past the car you asked about.
scenarios.jab: For just a little more a month, you could be in this one instead.

replies.line: I'm here for the one I asked about. Let's price that.
replies.why: It redirects to your target without debating the upgrade, which starves the upsell.
replies.delivery: Pause, then say “I'm here for the one I asked about” at a steady, conversational volume. ” without mocking the alternative.

replies.why: It refuses the redirect in four words and points back at your car.
replies.delivery: Say “Not that one” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. ” without mocking the alternative.

replies.line: It looks good, but I'd like to stay with the car and budget I chose.
replies.why: It receives the suggestion while holding the original purchase scope.
replies.delivery: Keep “It looks good, but I'd like to stay” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. ” without mocking the alternative.

replies.line: My budget and I are exclusive.
replies.why: It expresses commitment to your chosen budget through a light metaphor.
replies.delivery: Keep “My budget and I are exclusive” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. ” without mocking the alternative.

scenarios.goal: Keep an upsell focused on your chosen budget.

followUp.jab: It's practically the same monthly payment.
followUp.line: Please compare the total cost and terms for the car I chose.
followUp.why: It moves the comparison from monthly framing to the full purchase terms.
followUp.delivery: Point to the chosen car and stress “total cost,” without mocking the alternative.
